## Grammar

Basic word order is SOV; it has postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; noun before the adjective; demonstrative before the noun; noun before the numeral; relative clause before the noun. Overall it is head-final.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, split alignment (ergative in some contexts, accusative in others), no grammatical number, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past, future, perfective and habitual; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator after the verb; yes/no questions use an initial question particle. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; alienable and inalienable possession told apart; numeral classifiers; serial verbs; adjectives that behave like verbs; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a vigesimal counting base.
Measured morphology: 9 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.3 (0 free word … 3 fused), 4 paradigm cells, 4 of them with allomorphy.
